meaning: A creature. Everything that grows outgrows its shell, and the empty shell walks with the habits of what grew in it. The player keeps and battles them.
The coming-of-age day when a child's first shell comes off. Ouro has not turned yet. Also used for a world or a house leaving its shell.
A child who has not turned on time, or an adult who never did.
Forcing a second shell off later in life. Rare, and it hurts.
The shell a person leaves when they turn. Most children keep it as their first companion. A person's cast conjoins with nothing.
The world of Act 1: a great shell lying open to the sky.
The edge of the Volute. Ouro walks the Lip from Stay to Stay to turn.
One of eight enormous black things driven through the shell to hold the Volute shut. Each has a keeper and a hall with a puzzle.
The keeper of a Stay. The gym leader of each Stay hall. Beating one wins a pearl.
The high center of the Volute, where the Operculum sits.
The old mechanism at the Apex that sets the tension on all eight Stays. The name is the lid that seals a shell.
The person who turns the Operculum.
A fine black crack that opens in the ground where the shell pulls against itself. STONE whorls walk over them.
The Volute's last shell, lying beyond the northern Lip, from the one time it turned before.
The people who stayed on the Exuvia.
The shallow water past the Lip, where Cinch walked out and sat down.
A region at the world's edge.
A group, led by Bare, who think the Volute must turn. They catch big whorls to pull the Stays loose. Their base is the Hermitage.
Catching a wild whorl. A weakened whorl curls up into a horn. In battle the player picks Sound.
The device that catches a whorl. Periwinkle, whelk, triton, and nautilus horns, from weakest to strongest. Each has a line: the share of HP at which it always works.
A species of whorl. There are 250 kinds. Every kind has the same stat total, so a kind is its moves and habits.
The up to four whorls the player walks with. Characters say 'your four'.
The first whorl on the team. It walks with Ouro, comes out first in battle, and is the one Ouro wears.
Storage at every grotto for whorls not on the team. In the real world a midden is a heap of old shells.
The Strandmonger's book of every kind seen and sounded. The creature encyclopedia.
Climbing into the lead whorl, the way a hermit crab wears a shell, to cross ground its type allows. The player presses C.
Fusing two whorls into one new whorl. It keeps two moves from each parent and two habits. It cannot be undone.
The person at a grotto who conjoins whorls.
Where two conjoined whorls join. It takes a share from every stat of the new whorl.
A rare whorl with night-sky colors that glows and twinkles. The shiny variant.
A passive ability. Each whorl has two, and they work by themselves.
The building in every town with the shop, the Midden, the Nacre counter, and later the Conjoiner. The healing center and shop in one.
The person at the grotto counter.
A trader who prices everything, keeps the Register, and buys cowries on the Strand.
Money. Small shells.
The badge each Staykeeper gives. Each one raises the level cap and can be worn as a charm.
A pearl worn to help the whole team in battle. One at a time.
A held item. Each whorl holds one. Some have an action that works once a battle.
The shiny lining of a shell. Layered on a whorl at the grotto, each layer adds points to one stat.
A drawing that unlocks a new Setting puzzle.
The whorl fighting right now is out. The others wait in reserve.
The battle resource the whole team shares. Attacks and knockouts add tide, and crests spend it. In Act 2 it is also the sea that rises and falls on the Strand.
A whorl's biggest move. It costs tide.
A move that lands later. Stun, Silence, Sleep, Taunt, or a forced switch cuts it off.
Area damage. Splash 35% means each foe in reserve takes 35% of the hit.
Order classes. A Quick move goes first in a round. A Late move waits until the foe has moved.
Move types shown as icons, each with one rule. Guard does not stop a dash, it stops most of a projectile, Silence stops spells, and a channel keeps going on the next turns.
An action that halves damage until the whorl's next turn. It always goes first and cannot be used twice in a row.
A stacking sign a move or habit puts on a whorl, shown as a diamond by the HP bar. Each kind has its own marks.
A helper a whorl puts on the field. It acts by itself, and some guard their whorl.
A move effect that changes the whole battle for a few rounds, such as Sea Fog or High Tide.
A field that builds each turn. At 9 the ninth wave breaks over both out whorls.
After round 25, both out whorls lose a growing share of HP each round, slowest first, so no battle runs forever.
Stats: magic power, magic defense, speed, and charm. CHA helps horns and shortens the wait after a switch.
A status. The whorl cannot be knocked out and stays at 1 HP.
A status. The whorl skips its turns, and nothing can hurt it or give it a status.
The night beach of Act 2, where the shells of whole worlds lie in the sand.
A second level scale for Volute whorls on the Strand. It starts at 5.
What raises the Strand level cap. The Act 2 version of pearls.

match: low water|high water|dead low|spring low|the low|a low
meaning: The two states of the tide on the Strand. At low water stars fall. A spring low goes farthest out, and dead low is the lowest point.
What happens at the end of every low: every empty shell left out on the sand is gone.
Online play. The name is the threads a mussel uses to hold on to a rock.
A deduction minigame at every grotto: open a bed of clams without prising a cracked one.
A card duel on a three by three board, played with the whorls the player has sounded.
An Act 2 minigame played under the falling stars.
A puzzle board for setting gems. The player builds a machine of arms and stations that each follow a tape of steps.
